prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: sideswipe while changing lanes in Pasadena, Texas. Injury: concussion. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1205; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record yet. My attorney said we could handle identifying information separately.

Q: That's fine for now. Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was driving on the frontage road near Pasadena, Texas, heading toward my office. It was a weekday afternoon and traffic was moderate.

Q: Describe what happened immediately before the impact.
A: I was in the left lane and I was about to merge over to the right lane to make my exit. I checked my mirror, I saw the lane was clear, and I signaled. Then the other vehicle came up beside me and clipped my driver's side, right behind my front wheel.

Q: Did the other driver signal before changing lanes?
A: I didn't see a signal. I only heard a loud scrape and then felt my car pushed toward the curb.

Q: Did you hit your head at any point?
A: Yes. My head struck the driver's side window hard enough to crack the glass. I remember my ears ringing and everything looked a little blurry.

Q: What did you do after the collision?
A: I pulled onto the shoulder and sat there for a while. I felt dizzy and nauseated, and I couldn't focus on my phone when I tried to call someone. An ambulance came after a few minutes.

Q: When did you first seek medical treatment?
A: I went to the emergency room that same day. They did a CT scan and told me I had a concussion. They sent me home with instructions to rest.

Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: I've seen my primary care doctor several times and I've been referred to a neurologist. I also started physical therapy for my neck and balance problems. I had to stop going to the gym for a while because the doctor told me to avoid anything that made me feel worse.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: It's been hard. I get headaches most afternoons, and bright screens bother me. I used to read a lot and now I can only manage a few pages before my eyes feel tired. I've had to leave work early on some days, and my supervisor has been understanding but I know my productivity has dropped.

Q: Have you had any problems sleeping?
A: Yes. I have trouble falling asleep and I wake up several times a night. Before the accident I rarely had any sleep issues at all.

Q: Do you have any problems with memory or concentration?
A: Sometimes I lose my train of thought in the middle of a conversation. I write everything down now because I'm afraid I'll forget appointments.
